text: conditions: • Investigate more coatings and additives for composite tanks without liners • Measure laminate permeability under cryogenic and room temperature conditions • Explore barrier layer concept with HACNT’s embedded in a supported resin film on the laminate side exposed to cold temperature to reduce permeability • Create database of composite properties tested for cryogenic environments 6.0 Lessons Learned 1. No major technical obstacles were faced. The conformal tank concept design was completed ahead of schedule. The preliminary design of the Phase 1 tank was also completed ahead of schedule and the detailed design was almost complete at the time of program termination. 2. Some planning/logistics obstacles were faced and this was primarily due to the later start of the sub- contractor due to IP issues contributing in part. Technically, the program proceeded well and was ahead of schedule for the first 3 quarters. 3. One sub-contractor (Faurecia) did not join the program due their concern about US govt. restrictions on their international operations (in Europe and China). 4. The scope of testing at cryogenic temperatures needed to be made more efficient as the program developed. The test matrix involved various combinations of 2 composite layups, 2 ply architectures, without and with CNTs, at room and cryogenic temperatures, for static and fatigue testing. The testing schedule was speeded up by UDRI to make up for the delayed start, and significant progress was achieved in this regard. The remainder of the test matrix was reduced and made more targeted to desired layups, based on learnings from tests done prior in the program. However, it was not completed due to program termination. References: 1.
